gap: None of the three result pages I could open (StormWatts solar-input comparison, StormWatts kit comparison, MachineFanatic) states that the AC watt rating on these 5 kWh kits is tied to one outlet and voltage: Anker's own S5000 page caps every 120 V outlet at 3,600 W or less and gives the full 4,500 W only on the 240 V L14-30R, so that kit never reaches 5,000 W.
standout_why: StormWatts' 240 V solar-input page (cited in chat 1) lists every station only as '120/240 V' with no outlet ratings. StormWatts' kit page gives no 120 V or 240 V output figures at all. MachineFanatic gives only overall ratings and one unrelated 15 A input figure. The solar-side mechanism is already on StormWatts (Jackery's 4,000 W port is 135-450 V, its low-voltage ports are 10.5 A, about 876 W from portable panels), so that part scores 0. Caveat: the cited solargenreview.com page returned HTTP 429 on three tries and solargenadvisor.com failed on a certificate error, so I could not check either for outlet ratings.
decides: Read as 5,000 W of AC output, the Anker S5000 + 2x 400 W kit ($3,599.99) falls short: 4,500 W, and only on the 240 V L14-30R. It qualifies for the page on battery size (5,024 Wh) only. The BLUETTI 5kWh RV kits are the only kits we link whose maker page states 5,000 W continuous, but they are a wall-mounted install (drilling template, wood screws, distribution-panel wiring pack) with at most 600 W of panels in the listing. Jackery's 7,200 W Explorer 5000 Plus is a pre-order (station ships Dec 2, 500X panel by Dec 5), so it cannot be the ships-now pick. Shipping check needed before the Anker kit is called 'ships now': Anker's S5000 page today says orders placed on or after November 6 ship within 11-12 weeks and the 400 W panel ships separately, which conflicts with the 'ships now' entry in the kits table.
candidates: Jackery Solar Generator 5000 Plus (Explorer 5000 Plus + 2x SolarSaga 500 X)

The FAQ says most RV owners can install it with basic DIY skills. Arithmetic at rated output: 5,120 Wh / 600 W = 8.5 hours of full sun; real output is lower.

findings.label: Why the bundle's panels cannot use the 4,000 W solar port (StormWatts, citing Jackery's listing and FAQ)
findings.value: High-voltage port 135-450 V, 15 A, 4,000 W; two low-voltage ports 16-60 V, 10.5 A each (600 W one port, 1,200 W both); SolarSaga 500 X: 48.5 V Voc, 41.7 V / 12.0 A operating; StormWatts' portable-panel figure about 876 W
findings.source_title: 5 kWh-Class Solar Generators Compared on Solar Input (StormWatts)
findings.note: Arithmetic: 10.5 A x 41.7 V = 438 W per port, 876 W for two panels rated 1,000 W. StormWatts' kit page (https://stormwatts.com/articles/solar-generator-kits-compared-same-panel-watts/, read 2026-11-18) adds that Jackery's page says to connect the 500 X in parallel only, never in series. A rival already has this, so it scores 0 for standout.

findings.note: MachineFanatic also lists the Jackery 5000 Plus bundle as '2 x 200W included' and shows no prices.
